title: State, budgets, and trust boundaries
notes: 3 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: An agent is a controlled loop. Define: An action proposal must pass the harness before changing the environment. Walk through: State; transition; attempt budget; tool permissions; tool errors; approvals; trace evidence. Ask: Where does the model lose authority? Expected answer and boundary: At every deterministic gate. A proposal cannot change the action set or enlarge its own budget. Visual purpose: show Observe > Propose > Validate > Act > Verify > Stop. Facilitation: ask students for a prediction before execution, locate the actual intermediate values, and distinguish observation from interpretation. Transition: connect this checked mechanism to the next beat; preserve the lab artifact where requested. title: Workflow and agent are not synonyms
notes: 2 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: Workflow and agent are not synonyms. Define: A fixed graph is a workflow; model-directed choices add an agent decision layer. Walk through: A three-step measurement report can use a script. Do not add open-ended planning when the steps are known. Ask: Does a loop alone make a system an LLM agent? Expected answer and boundary: No. The core notebook is a deterministic harness simulator. The language-model decision component is deliberately absent. Visual purpose: show Fixed route | Model-selected route | Same enforced boundary. Facilitation: ask students for a prediction before execution, locate the actual intermediate values, and distinguish observation from interpretation. title: Budgets need an accounting unit
notes: 2 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: Budgets need an accounting unit. Define: Count attempts, tool calls and declared work separately. Walk through: Three invalid proposals under a two-attempt cap must stop at the cap even though no tool ran. Ask: Can a tool-call cap guarantee short runtime? Expected answer and boundary: No. One call may hang or be expensive. Wall-clock limits and resource isolation are distinct controls. Visual purpose: show Attempt count | Dispatch count | Work limit. Facilitation: ask students for a prediction before execution, locate the actual intermediate values, and distinguish observation from interpretation. Transition: connect this checked mechanism to the next beat; preserve the lab artifact where requested. title: Use typed errors with narrow recovery
notes: 2 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: Use typed errors with narrow recovery. Define: Invalid input, transient tool failure and permission failure need different next steps. Walk through: A bounded retry can handle a simulated transient error; it cannot authorize a forbidden operation. Ask: Why can retries make behavior worse? Expected answer and boundary: Repeated side effects, cost and duplicate operations may occur. Retry only a declared safe operation with a bound. Visual purpose: show Invalid input | Transient error | Permission denial. Facilitation: ask students for a prediction before execution, locate the actual intermediate values, and distinguish observation from interpretation. title: Approval must name the exact action
notes: 2 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: Approval must name the exact action. Define: Bind action, arguments and a unique nonce into a reviewed digest. Walk through: An approval for draft A cannot be reused for draft B with different content or destination. Ask: Why is an 'approved=true' field insufficient? Expected answer and boundary: Untrusted callers could set it themselves. Approval must come from a separate authority and be checked against the exact request. Visual purpose: show Action + Args + Nonce > Digest > Reviewer approval.
